skill.name: security-and-hardening
skill.description: Hardens code against vulnerabilities. Use when auditing an input handler for vulnerabilities, when handling user input, authentication, data storage, or external integrations, or when checking a login flow is safe against the OWASP Top Ten. Use when building any feature that accepts untrusted data, manages user sessions, or interacts with third-party services. Use when auditing dependencies for known vulnerabilities, triaging package-manager audit findings, or assessing supply-chain risk in a new package. Use when personal data or privacy compliance (GDPR, CCPA) is involved.
skill.summary: Apply threat modeling, OWASP controls, secure input handling, dependency checks, and privacy safeguards while designing or reviewing applications.
skill.author: addyosmani

security_audit.summary: All 96 findings are false positives from examples and Markdown in SKILL.md. No executable behavior or prompt injection was found.

remediation.issue: Security scanners interpret defensive code examples as executable behavior.
remediation.suggestion: Fence examples clearly and label unsafe snippets as guidance. Review any scanner exclusions whenever the skill changes.

remediation.issue: The skill gives broad security guidance but does not verify a target application's implementation.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to validate recommendations against their framework, deployment topology, threat model, and runtime tests before relying on them.

content.value_statement: Security reviews can miss trust boundaries and unsafe data flows. This skill supplies threat-modeling prompts, OWASP patterns, and practical review checklists.
actual_capabilities: Maps trust boundaries and abuse cases with a lightweight STRIDE review.
Explains defensive patterns for authentication, authorization, input validation, XSS, SSRF, and security headers.
Reviews file uploads, destructive filesystem paths, secrets management, and personal-data handling.
Provides dependency-audit and package-install guidance for reachable vulnerabilities and supply-chain risks.
Applies security checks to LLM output, tool permissions, prompts, retrieval data, and resource limits.
Produces practical security checklists and verification questions for implementation reviews.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, but it does not execute scans or test a live application.
Recommendations require adaptation to the application framework, deployment topology, and threat model.
It cannot prove that dependencies, infrastructure, secrets, or authorization rules are secure.
Legal, compliance, and incident-response decisions require qualified human review.

use_cases.title: Review a New API Endpoint
use_cases.description: Map trust boundaries, validate request data, check authorization, and identify abuse cases before shipping an endpoint.

use_cases.title: Assess a Dependency Update
use_cases.description: Triage audit results by reachability, review install scripts and provenance, and define a documented remediation decision.

use_cases.title: Secure an AI Feature
use_cases.description: Evaluate prompt injection, unsafe model output, excessive tool permissions, data exposure, and unbounded consumption risks.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Security Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this feature for trust boundaries, untrusted inputs, authentication, authorization, and sensitive data exposure. List the three most important fixes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a first-pass review of a small feature.

prompt_templates.title: OWASP Endpoint Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this API endpoint against relevant OWASP risks. Check validation, queries, output encoding, access control, rate limits, errors, and logging. Cite issues and propose fixes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before merging a user-facing route.

prompt_templates.title: Dependency Risk Triage
prompt_templates.prompt: Triage these package audit results. Check reachability, available fixes, install scripts, provenance, and lockfile impact. Recommend an action and review date.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use during dependency upgrades or release preparation.

prompt_templates.title: AI System Threat Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Threat-model this LLM feature. Analyze prompt injection, unsafe output, data exposure, tool permissions, retrieval isolation, SSRF, limits, and irreversible actions. Prioritize controls and tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for an agent, RAG pipeline, chatbot, or model-powered automation.

output_examples.input: Review an endpoint that accepts a webhook URL and fetches it on behalf of a user.
output: Risk: The server may be vulnerable to SSRF if it fetches arbitrary user-supplied URLs.
Control: Allowlist HTTPS hosts, resolve all addresses, reject private or reserved ranges, and disable redirects.
Verification: Test loopback, link-local, private IPv4, IPv6, redirect, and DNS-rebinding cases.

output_examples.input: Assess an LLM feature that renders model replies in a web page.
output: Risk: Model output is untrusted and may become stored XSS when inserted as HTML.
Control: Encode output as text by default, or sanitize approved markup before rendering.
Verification: Test script payloads, event handlers, malformed markup, and content from retrieved documents.

output_examples.input: Triage a high-severity package advisory from a native package-manager audit.
output: Decision: Confirm whether the vulnerable function is reachable in production, build, test, or deployment paths.
Action: Update to a patched version when available, review the lockfile diff, and test the resulting dependency graph.
Exception: Document a temporary deferral, mitigation, owner, and review date when the vulnerable path is confirmed unused.

best_practices: Start with assets, trust boundaries, abuse cases, and authorization assumptions before choosing controls.
Treat user input, external responses, files, environment values, and model output as untrusted until validated.
Pair every recommendation with an implementation check, a negative test, and an owner for follow-up.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a prompt, client-side check, framework default, or internal network as a complete security boundary.
Do not pass untrusted data into SQL, shells, eval, HTML, file paths, or privileged tools without strict validation.
Do not accept audit results, dependency signatures, or compliance claims as proof without checking reachability and context.

faq.question: Does this skill scan my repository?
faq.answer: No. It provides review guidance and checklists. Use dedicated scanners and human review to inspect repository and runtime behavior.

faq.question: Which security topics does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers threat modeling, OWASP risks, authentication, authorization, input validation, XSS, SSRF, files, secrets, privacy, dependencies, and LLM features.

faq.question: Can it replace a penetration test?
faq.answer: No. It supports design and code review but cannot replace penetration testing, configuration review, monitoring, or incident exercises.

faq.question: How should I use its code examples?
faq.answer: Treat examples as patterns to adapt. Confirm framework behavior, error handling, permissions, deployment assumptions, and tests before using them.

faq.question: Can it assess dependency vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps triage reachability, fix availability, install scripts, provenance, lockfiles, and documented exceptions. Run the native package-manager audit separately.

faq.question: How does it address AI security?
faq.answer: It treats prompts, retrieved content, and model output as untrusted and reviews tool scope, data isolation, validation, confirmation, and consumption limits.
